{
  "question_intent": "Bank earnings-call question on NIM and Markets VAR",
  "main_topics": ["US cards NIM", "Markets VAR"],
  "answer_completeness": "Complete",
  "response_stance": "Direct",
  "evidence_level": "High",
  "contains_numeric_evidence": true,
  "contains_forward_guidance": false,
  "narrative_alignment": "Aligned",
  "question_quote": "Sheel Shah, JP Morgan. First, in the US cards, coming back to the NIM. Can I ask if you think that greater than 12% is still achievable for 2026, given you're holding maybe a bit more excess liquidity from deposits, revolver balances are maybe a little lower than you'd expect?",
  "answer_quote": "Let me start with US cards, yes, we believe it's [still] achievable. What you're seeing in Q1 is a slightly odd picture, impacted by a couple of things. The first is, as Fed rates reduce in any particular quarter, you're going to see some degree of compression in NIM, but then offset in non-interest income. We've got floating rate assets, largely fixed rate liabilities that take time to reprice. We do hedge the position, but it's not the kind of structural hedging that you see within BUK, and the income from that hedge actually flows into non-NII. So it's a little bit messy, but you can see year-on-year that non-NII is much stronger, and that's really the effect of that hedge. But on an underlying basis, no real pressure on income. The other thing that's going on in Q1 is, what I would describe as a full NIM, it's not a banking NIM. So we have some cash sitting on the balance sheet ready to do a securitisation repayment, and that's undermined the NIM by creating a larger denominator. [The] pathway from here, I can see clear building blocks to get us to that greater than 12% position, and they come from all of the areas that we talked about before. So, the repricing that was completed last year, and flows through into NIM as customers use those cards and pay down the pre-repriced balances. The second thing is the deposits that we talked about previously. Thirdly is just the overall risk mix, clearly we'll get another move on again once we onboard [General Motors] later in the year. The building blocks are still in place, Sheel, so we're comfortable with that progress, it's a really key part of our plan. In terms of Markets VaR, I wouldn't call anything [out] in particular, because it's actually a business style and philosophy across the entirety of the market business. Again, it reflects the strategy that we set out at the beginning of this planning cycle for you, which was a real focus on the fact that we had deployed a lot of technology into the Markets business. That means that we're taking more risk intra-day, not so much in terms of inventory. So that's really the thematic, you could see that across a number of businesses, and it's really a reflection of the investments that we've made. So when I say we've monetised the opportunity within the current environment, that's really what I'm talking about here, and we have been really nimble in the way that we deployed capital. So I wouldn't say anything more specific than that. Thank you.",
